content:
- Overestimate prices in the short term (1-3 days) after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overreact.
- Underestimate prices after negative sentiment periods; model is overly cautious and underweights downward momentum.
- Overshoot upward after strong positive sentiment; model fails to account for sentiment decay or policy-induced volatility.
- Underestimate downward moves after strong negative sentiment; model underweights risk or fails to recognize policy tightening.
- Mean-reversion bias: model overweights recent trends, especially in the 10-15 day horizon, ignoring longer-term equilibrium.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are consistently too high in early periods (first 5-7 days) when sentiment is positive, then converge — model lags in capturing sentiment-driven momentum shifts.
- Sentiment decay matters: if sentiment turns negative after a spike, model fails to adjust downward quickly; if sentiment turns positive after a dip, model overcorrects upward.
